steps.text: In a glass or ceramic bowl, stir together cornstarch, sugar, and salt. Mix in water. Heat in the microwave until mixture is thick and clear, about 2 minutes at full power. Set aside to cool slightly.

Beat egg whites in a large glass or metal bowl until foamy. Gradually pour in sugar mixture while continuing to whip egg whites until thick and stiff, enough to hold a peak. Cover pie filling completely with meringue, sealing to the edges. Bake as directed in the recipe, or in a preheated 450 degrees F (220 degrees C) oven until golden brown, 7 to 8 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: High Altitude Meringue for Pie
raw_recipe.description: This high altitude meringue recipe takes your pie meringues from flat and weepy to stable and full of volume. Works great with all pie flavors!

review.reviewBody: This meringue came out fabulous, and was so easy. After having the pie in the fridge overnight there was no weeping either. The taste was spot on! Thank you!

I'm in Santa Fe, NM at 7,500 feet above sea level and this recipe is a real Godsend for me. Anyone who can't make this meringue work just isn't doing it right. It's a genius idea to use that cup of water and cornstarch and while I was skeptical, at first, mine turned out perfectly. The key is to thicken the cornstarch/water solution in the microwave to the point where it's almost the thickness of honey. Cornstarch is a standard go to thickening agent and it's activated by heat, so be sure to heat it for at least 2 minutes or even 2 1/2 minutes to get it hot enough to activate. After the microwave I put the bowl into an ice water bath to cool it a little faster. I'm so very grateful to the poster of this recipe as it never would have occurred to me to invent this workaround. Cream of tartar is fine if you're at a low altitude, but it just doesn't work up high like Santa Fe. From the moment I was finished beating the egg whites it was obvious that the beaten meringue was a different consistency. While spreading it on top of my chocolate meringue pie I could tell there was less air in it and seemed heavier, which made it very smooth and manageable. Remember to use the back of a spoon to make the peaks before sticking it in the oven. John

This is the cat's meow!!! Sensational. I tried the Cook's Illustrated version and this one is better. You can't mess this one up. The meringue whips into a nice tall meringue. The meringue on my left-over chocolate cream pie still looked picture-pretty the next day. 
The only change I made was to add 1/2 teaspoon Cream of Tarter. Not sure if it really made any difference.

I live at 9,000 ft. and have always had an issue with meringue, but this recipe worked great! I did microwave for 2:30, then let the cornstarch mixture cool for about 10 minutes, and then added. Perfect!
Really the best lemon meringue I’ve ever had. The lemon flavor did not disappoint.
Delicious and it works great! Super easy fix. We are at 6200 feet elevation

I cannot understand how this recipe received 5 star reviews. This recipe produces the most pathetic meringue I have ever seen. I should have known when it called for water. It shrunk and collapsed and turned my beautiful coconut cream pie into a watery mess. The only reason I give it 1 star is because I cannot give it zero stars.
We team tagged beating it for 30 minutes! There was no mention of how long it would take

I live near Denver, CO, so a mile high. This recipe came out great - nice and fluffy and tall, and holding it's shape well after a couple of days in the fridge. I highly recommend this for high altitude!

oh my gosh,I just tried your recipe and it worked magnificently. The pie meringue I have been trying to make for years never turns out. You stated it correctly , weepy and flat. My husbands homemade coconut cream pie looks fantastic for his birthday today. Thank you so much for submitting your technique for bakers like me who never give up on perfecting merinque.
Excellent recipe. Used it up on the top of a mountain and at sea level. Works great both places. No more weepy meringue.

I just made this to go on top of a banana pudding, it is great. I followed it exactly except that I made a double batch. I found out after doubling it I did not need to this makes enough for a 9x13 pan. The recipe is easy and for the first time I made great Meringue, I had peaks and all. Thank you so much for sharing.

My family loves a lemon meringue pie but the next day most of the meringue has fallen or turned weepy. I decided to try this and it was fabulous! 5 star fabulous. Easy to make and firm fluffy peaks of meringue sat on top of my pie. The next night the meringue tasted just as good and still looked fabulous! I'm going to make all my meringues this way from now on!
